extracted.intended_audience: readers of Popular Science Monthly: scientifically literate public, educators, and practicing scientists/engineers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative guidance for assessing scientific claims (e.g., clairvoyance, experiments, photographs, devices) and for judging the quality/usability of scientific books and manuals. Emphasizes demonstrability, pedagogy, practical utility, and fidelity of evidence or instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific discoveries must produce procurable effects
rubrics_metrics.description: "All scientific discoveries, in fact, are new procurable effects, and are, therefore, their own witnesses."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A genuine discovery should immediately yield effects or results that can be obtained and demonstrated; while long-term applications may lag, the immediate consequences of the discovery should be observable and attest its reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not claim new faculties without new revelations
rubrics_metrics.description: "With a new capacity for seeing, what new thing has been seen?... Clairvoyance has given no help in conquering these difficulties."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of extraordinary faculties (e.g., clairvoyance) must be judged by whether they reveal facts or phenomena inaccessible to ordinary methods; merely restating what is already known is insufficient evidence of a new faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof must be positive, demonstrable, and open to science
rubrics_metrics.description: "The proof is not the mere testimony of a few parties... but what has been positively, and demonstrably, and openly gained to science?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim's credibility depends on reproducible, demonstrable results presented openly for scientific scrutiny rather than on isolated testimony or anecdotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use controlled, supervised experiments to test extraordinary claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: M. Burdin placed money with a notary and appointed an Academy committee to supervise experiments in an opaque box to test clairvoyance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests should be designed to eliminate ordinary explanations and fraud (opaque containers, independent supervision, varying conditions, clear success criteria, sufficient time for challengers). Negative results and detection of fraudulent methods are informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary claims must yield new, confirmable scientific facts (not just confirmations)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The new way of getting into the mysteries of the organism should have attested itself by results not accessible by ordinary means."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations that claim novel capacities must produce results that extend the boundaries of knowledge — e.g., revealing internal conditions or phenomena previously unknown and later confirmable (e.g., by post-mortem examination under controlled conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific photographs should both confirm and add to observational knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: On M. Janssen's solar photographs: they "constitute a most essential step in the study of the sun" because they confirm optical observations and "present new facts, such as the evidence of storms upon the solar surface."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality scientific imagery should corroborate prior observations while also providing novel, verifiable information; such images should be disseminated to the scientific community for further study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and reproducibility of results (including images) are essential
rubrics_metrics.description: "These admirable photographs can hardly fail to soon become known, by copies to the scientific public..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important experimental or observational results (photographs, data) should be circulated to the relevant scientific community so others can examine, reproduce, and build on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate mechanical/acoustical devices by fidelity to original phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: About the phonograph: "The voice... is somewhat muffled and minified when returned... but its intonations, inflections, pauses, and quality, are rendered with surprising fidelity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess instruments (e.g., phonographs) by how accurately they reproduce salient features (intonation, inflection, pause timing, timbre) of the original; note any consistent distortions (muffling, minification) and their practical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbooks for beginners should appeal to observation and start from familiar facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Huxley: "the attempt to convey scientific conceptions without the appeal to observation... appears to me to be in direct antagonism to the fundamental principles of scientific education."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational works should begin with local/familiar phenomena, use observation as the basis for concepts, lead learners step-by-step to more abstract ideas, and cultivate understanding progressively as knowledge 'grows' from experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching texts should be accessible to primary-school learners while retaining scientific precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Huxley aimed to convey scientific method and 'some practical experience of scientific method... without overstepping the comprehension of learners... who pass through an ordinary primary school.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good pedagogical texts balance precision with accessibility: clear statements, examples from everyday experience, and scaffolding toward more complex topics so beginners can follow without technical prerequisites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical works should be locally transferable and well illustrated
rubrics_metrics.description: "He began by ideally placing his audience upon London Bridge... the book has a flavor of locality, but the thoughtful teacher in using it will simply transfer its applications to his own region." Also: "The book is beautifully illustrated."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective school texts use place-based examples that teachers can adapt to their region and include good illustrations to aid comprehension and serve as class-book or reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly essays intended for wider audiences should be shaped to affect readers appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: On Chauncey Wright: his pieces "were rather studies than finished work... they lacked proportion, relief, perspective... he never knew how to sink himself in his subject... to accommodate the workings of his own mind to [readers'] needs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For essays aiming to influence beyond specialist circles, authors should edit and structure material for proportion, clarity, and perspective so it communicates effectively to the intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical manuals must supply formulae and usable data for engineering application
rubrics_metrics.description: A Manual of Heating and Ventilation: "to furnish... the formulae and data necessary for computing the dimensions and determining the other conditions of heating and ventilating appliances."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engineering/technical manuals should prioritize practical applicability: provide formulas, data, and computational procedures that practitioners (engineers, architects) can directly apply to design and sizing tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical/scientific books should be systematic, student-friendly, and clarify notational differences
rubrics_metrics.description: On Fleischer's volumetric analysis: "a systematic work... accepted as a standard in Germany... the translator thinks that the putting of the two notations, side by side, will be useful as disclosing the superiority of the newer plan."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Texts intended for instruction should be organized systematically, serve students' learning needs, and where possible present multiple notations/approaches side-by-side to help readers understand transitions in practice and theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference/scientific volumes should combine clear exposition with quality illustrations/plates
rubrics_metrics.description: On Manual of Inorganic Chemistry and Contributions to North American Ethnology: clear descriptions "efficiently supplemented by numerous well-executed wood engravings"; ethnology volume includes numerous plates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity of exposition plus well-executed visual material (engravings, plates, maps) enhances usability and value for both specialists and amateurs; visual aids are especially important in descriptive sciences (mineralogy, ethnology, archaeology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Introductory field guides should be concise, comprehensive, and include practical identification methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Guide to the Determination of Rocks: "a plain, brief, but comprehensive introduction... Part III, giving the method to be followed in the practical determination of rocks, will be found of especial value to beginners."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good field guides provide succinct, comprehensive descriptions, English synonyms where helpful, and clear step-by-step practical methods for identification targeting beginners and amateurs.
